A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adaptive Guided Erasure (AGE) research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A-D are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-space analyses and experiments on object, nudity, and artistic-style erasure, together with appendix ablations, scalability tests, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical analyses and experimental results, including the supplementary evaluations in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same minimax objective, Gumbel-Softmax target mixtures, candidate filtering, and alternating updates in Algorithm 1. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same NetFive and Imagenette object concepts, I2P prompts, five artistic styles, and COCO 30K preservation evaluation. The appendix scalability and synonym test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within the corresponding experiments, including ESD, UCE, CA, MACE, and AP in Tables 1 and 6, and ESD/UCE in the scalability comparison. AP's citation changes from Bui et al. 2024b to 2024a without changing the evaluated method.

E3.justification: The same model versions, training settings, metrics, and evaluation procedures are reported. Both retain 1000-step fine-tuning, four five-class Imagenette erasure tasks with 500 images per class, and the 4703-image I2P evaluation.

E4.justification: The concept-impact analyses and Appendix D investigations are retained unchanged: vocabulary selection, hyperparameter sensitivity, scalability, concept mixtures, target-search trajectories, synonym robustness, and qualitative comparisons.

E5.justification: The same plus/minus statistics and plotted error bars appear in both versions. Section 5.3 retains five seeds per artistic-style prompt; no seed information, repeated-run disclosure, significance testing, or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted results, and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, both Table 1 versions report AGE ESR-5 of 95.7 ± 2.5 and PSR-5 of 95.6 ± 1.1; Table 2 retains NER-0.5 of 1.53 and FID of 14.20. Image-resolution changes do not introduce new experimental outputs.

T1.justification: The concept-impact definitions, Equations 1-5, minimax formulation, and mathematical explanations in the appendices are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about localized concept-erasure effects, adaptive target selection, and improved preservation while maintaining effective erasure. The stated contributions and novelty scope do not change.

C2.justification: Interpretations of locality, target selection, vocabulary effects, and erasure-preservation tradeoffs remain unchanged. Appendix B retains the computational-cost limitation of large concept spaces and the limitation involving nonsmooth concept mixtures.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hyperparameters, candidate-selection details, and data-construction instructions remain unchanged. The code and data pointers, including their external hyperlink targets, are also identical.

R1.justification: The Bui learnable-prompts reference is updated from 'Removing undesirable concepts...' to 'Hiding and recovering knowledge...' with workshop metadata and the same author group and citation role. Associated a/b suffixes change, but related-work coverage and the research positioning in Appendix A remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited author-block, citation-label, and bibliography edits, with text reflow around resized figures. Section organization and substantive prose remain unchanged. Appendix D.4 introduces a cross-reference error: v1's 'Table 7' becomes 'Table ??' in v3.

P2.justification: Figures 3 and 5 are slightly enlarged and repositioned, affecting adjacent text and caption layout. Several qualitative image panels have higher raster resolution, and image encoding changes throughout. The figure/table inventory, display structures, axes, and scientific content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 retains the same scientific argument, methods, evidence, and limitations. Slightly larger charts, higher-resolution image panels, and updated bibliography metadata provide small presentational benefits, while 'Table ??' introduces a minor defect; the correctly numbered Table 7 remains immediately below it. These limited changes do not materially alter the paper's overall clarity or evidential strength.
